prompt: Use case: art-direction redesign of a real in-game frame. Image 1 is the game today: keep its camera, horizon, field of view, the volcano's exact silhouette and outline, its ridges and gullies, and everything in the foreground (houses, roofs, hills, woods, clouds) exactly where they are. Image 2 shows the game's art direction: soft painterly low-poly shapes, flat matte shading, a clean blue sky. Repaint only the volcano's surface so it looks beautiful and natural from afar: faceted cool lavender-grey volcanic rock with visible crags, cliff bands and outcrops; snow lying in the gullies as thin, irregular, branching streaks that taper downhill and break up among the rocks, heavier just under the rim and fading out lower down - no evenly spaced stripes, no blobs, no shapes that read as letters; below the rock, scree and alpine scrub, then autumn forest (orange, gold and dark green pines) climbing the lower flanks with soft natural edges. The view north from the edge of the coastal city, the volcano 2 km away. The woods must not look patchy: no hard-edged carpets or blobs of trees on bare lawn. Instead one continuous, natural autumn forest of mixed pines, maples and ginkgos covers the foothills and lower flanks, its canopy varied in colour (orange, gold, dark green) with soft, irregular edges; it thins gradually upslope into scattered single trees and small groups among scrub and meadow, then scree and rock, with only a few natural meadow clearings. The two foreground wood patches become part of that forest, blending into the hillside instead of sitting on it.
